title: Spreadsheet formula engine (hard, parsing + dependency graph)
command:
Implement the spreadsheet engine in sheet.py (standard library only). Public API: Sheet().set(cell, text), Sheet().get(cell) -> value, Sheet().formula(cell) -> the raw text last set ("" if never set). Cell names are case-insensitive ("a1" == "A1"), column A..ZZ, row 1..9999.

Cell contents
- Unset or "" is empty: get() returns None.
- Text starting with "=" is a formula.
- Otherwise, if the text (ignoring surrounding whitespace) is a number such as "5", "-3.5", "1e3", the value is that number; anything else is kept as a text value, unchanged.
- Numbers are returned as Python numbers (int or float, compared numerically).

Formulas
- Literals: numbers, strings in double quotes ("" inside a string is one quote), TRUE and FALSE (case-insensitive).
- References: A1, $A$1, a1 ($ markers are ignored). Ranges like A1:B3 are allowed only as function arguments.
- Operators, lowest to highest precedence: comparisons = <> < <= > >= ; & (text join) ; + - ; * / ; ^ ; unary + and -. All binary operators are left-associative, so 2^3^2 = 64, and unary minus binds tighter than ^, so -2^2 = 4. Parentheses group.
- Functions (names case-insensitive): SUM, MIN, MAX, AVERAGE, COUNT, IF(cond, a, b), ROUND(x, digits), LEN(text), CONCAT(a, ...).
- Values in arithmetic and comparisons: empty counts as 0 (or "" when compared with text); TRUE/FALSE count as 1/0; text in arithmetic is #VALUE!.
- & and CONCAT turn values into text: whole numbers without decimals (5 -> "5", 2.0 -> "2"), other numbers with format(x, ".15g"), booleans as TRUE/FALSE, empty as "".
- Comparisons return TRUE/FALSE. Two texts compare case-insensitively; numbers/booleans/empty compare numerically; a number against text is #VALUE!.
- SUM, MIN, MAX, AVERAGE, COUNT: inside ranges, only numbers count (empty, text and booleans are skipped); a direct argument that is empty is skipped, a number or boolean counts, and text is #VALUE!. MIN and MAX of nothing are 0. AVERAGE of nothing is #DIV/0!. COUNT counts numbers in ranges and number/boolean direct arguments.
- IF: cond is true when it is a nonzero number or TRUE (text cond is #VALUE!). Only the chosen branch is evaluated, so an error in the other branch does not matter. IF with two arguments returns FALSE when cond is false.
- ROUND rounds half away from zero; digits may be negative (ROUND(1250, -2) = 1300). LEN returns the length of the value as text.

Errors (get() returns these strings)
- "#DIV/0!" division by zero; "#VALUE!" wrong type; "#NAME?" unknown function or wrong argument count; "#REF!" a reference outside A1..ZZ9999 (such as A0); "#PARSE!" a formula that cannot be parsed; "#CYCLE!" for every cell on a reference cycle and every cell that references (directly or indirectly) a cell with #CYCLE!.
- Any error used as an operand or function argument makes the result that error; with several, the leftmost one in the formula wins.

Recalculation: get() always reflects the current contents after any set(). Long dependency chains must work: a chain of 3000 cells (A2 = A1+1, A3 = A2+1, ...) must evaluate without RecursionError and quickly.
